US-119-HR10909.title: Deaths in Custody Reporting Reform Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committees on Homeland Security, and Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10909.description: To amend the Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013 to require submission of reports to the Director of the Bureau of Justice Statistics, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10909.aiSummary: The bill would change how deaths in custody are reported under the 2013 law. It would require more detailed reports to the Director of the Bureau of Justice Statistics, including more facts about each death, and it would call for a public database and yearly reports. It would also direct the National Institute of Justice to study the data and report its findings to Congress.

US-119-S5649.title: Alaska Native Vietnam Era Veterans Land Allotment Fulfillment Act of 2026

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5649.description: A bill to make additional Federal public land available for selection under the Alaska Native Vietnam era veterans land allotment program, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5649.aiSummary: The bill would make more federal land in Alaska available for selection under the Alaska Native Vietnam era veterans land allotment program. It would require the Interior Secretary to open certain wildlife refuge lands right away, and it would direct the Agriculture Secretary to identify more Forest Service land within one year. The changes would affect eligible Alaska Native Vietnam era veterans seeking land allotments.

US-119-S5627.title: John Lewis Equality in Medicare and Medicaid Treatment Act of 2026
US-119-S5627.summary:
John Lewis Equality in Medicare and Medicaid Treatment Act of 2026

This bill requires the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a payment model that addresses social determinants of health and health disparities, particularly with respect to minorities, underserved areas, and high-risk individuals. The bill also generally incorporates consideration of such factors into the selection, implementation, and evaluation of other models, including the decision as to whether to expand a model's duration and scope.
US-119-S5627.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2026-09-30)

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5627.aiSummary: The bill would require the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a payment model that looks at social factors that affect health and health gaps. It would focus on minorities, underserved areas, and people at high risk. It would also tell the agency to take these factors into account when choosing, running, and reviewing other payment models.

US-119-HJRES210.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision".
US-119-HJRES210.summary:
This joint resolution revokes the authorization granted to the California Air Resources Board (CARB) to amend its Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth Regulation. Among other elements, the amendment proposed by CARB and authorized by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) expanded auxiliary engine emissions reductions requirements to include additional categories of ocean-going vessels. (Under the Clean Air Act, the EPA may authorize California to adopt and enforce standards relating to the control of emissions from nonroad vehicles or engines if those standards meet certain requirements.)

Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the EPA authorization decision titled California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision .

US-119-S4659.title: Election Security Partnership Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4659.description: A bill to provide additional election security funding to States providing voter registration information to the Department of Homeland Security.
US-119-S4659.aiSummary: The bill would give the Election Assistance Commission $20 million more for election security grants. States could get this money if they got a 2026 election security grant and sign an agreement to share their full voter registration list with the Department of Homeland Security at least every three months after September 30, 2026. The extra payment to each state could not be more than 10% of what it got from the 2026 grant program.

US-119-HR1912.title: Veteran Fraud Reimbursement Act of 2025
US-119-HR1912.summary:
Veteran Fraud Reimbursement Act of 2025

This act modifies the procedures by which the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) reissues misused benefits to a beneficiary, including by requiring the VA to establish methods and timing with respect to determining whether an instance of misuse by a fiduciary is the result of negligence by the VA. The act also provides that if a beneficiary predeceases a reissuance, the VA must pay the amount to a surviving beneficiary in the same method as certain other VA benefits are paid upon the death of a beneficiary.

Under the act, the VA may not withhold the reissuing of a benefit payment by reason of a pending determination regarding the VA's negligence in relation to the instance of misuse by a fiduciary. Additionally, the VA is not required to make a determination regarding its negligence for each instance of misuse by a fiduciary of all or part of an individual's benefit paid to such fiduciary.

US-119-HR1912.aiSummary: The law changes how the Department of Veterans Affairs reissues benefits that were misused by a fiduciary, or person who manages benefits for someone else. It requires the VA to set rules for when and how it decides whether the misuse happened because of VA negligence, but the VA cannot delay reissuing the payment while that decision is pending. If the beneficiary dies before the payment is reissued, the VA must pay the amount to a surviving beneficiary in the same way it pays certain other VA benefits after death.

US-119-HJRES61.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing".
US-119-HJRES61.summary: This joint resolution removes emission regulations on hazardous air pollutants under the rubber tire manufacturing source category, specifically from the rubber processing subcategory. The joint resolution nullifies the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) rule titled National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing , which addresses the decision in Louisiana Environmental Action Network v. EPA (D.C. Cir. 2020) that requires the EPA to address unregulated emissions from a major source category when it conducts the 8-year technology review. The rule implemented emissions standards for the rubber processing subcategory.
